- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast drop to 5–10% below peak to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day weighted average) to reduce volatility amplification.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1.00, -0.33, 1.00), model often misreads trend direction; favor sentiment-weighted average over pure trend-following.
